rationale: The candidate reads coherently across views as a single rectilinear bar with one small roof volume, so gesture clarity and repair integrity are acceptable. However, the mass is still fundamentally generic and box-like, with the roof appendage not yet resolving into a convincing program section. The carved south-side void is visible, but it is shallow and does not strongly register as a public court or active threshold responding to the verified access edge; in the top and front views the building remains sealed and semantically passive at grade. For neighborhood living, the visible form does not yet support a clear active ground edge, mixed-use public threshold, or upper/ground hierarchy strong enough to pass program fit. The silhouette is not bad, but it is more a block with a token rooftop extrusion than a capacity-bearing inhabited section. The main corrective direction is to keep the bar anchor, but deepen the access-side void and convert the upper piece into a more legible profiled/sectional move rather than a minor box on top.
